title: Candidate profile: Adrienne Scritsmier hopes to move the needle on the Wilsonville council - NewsBreak
text:
By Mac Larsen ,
21 hours ago The Review is running profiles of all City Council candidates in Lake Oswego, West Linn and Wilsonville prior to the November election.
When Adrienne Scritsmier was a fifth grader, she didn’t know that she was planting the seeds that would blossom into her candidacy for Wilsonville City Council.
In the fifth grade, while attending Boeckman Creek Primary School, she traveled to Kitakata, Japan – Wilsonville’s sister city. In 2020, when the nonprofit organization that ran the sister city relationship was at risk of shuttering, she knew she had to get involved on the nascent Kitakata Sister City Advisory Board.
“It’s just a really special relationship that we have with Kitakata, and that’s really what got me civically engaged upon moving back to Wilsonville,” said Scritmister.
Scritmister works for Clackamas Community College as a community education coordinator. She has served on the Kitakata Sister City Committee and was appointed to the budget committee in December 2025. A graduate of Wilsonville High School, she returned to the community to raise a family.
“I’ve spent years serving this community and, as an educator and through my local volunteer work, I care about making sure Wilsonville continues to be a place where people at different stages of life can afford to live, feel included and see a future for themselves,” said Scritsmier.
If elected, she hopes to focus on infrastructure, transportation improvements and sustainable growth.
“We’ve got some growing pains and challenges, and it’s just part of being a younger city and a city that has grown and expanded rapidly, in my opinion,” said Scritsmier.
She also wants to expand access to city resources and social services. However, she said the new 10x bus route to Clackamas Town Center has been helpful in this regard.
Establishing a direction for the future of Town Center that the entire community can feel confident about, though, is her top priority for the new City Council. Growing up in town, she said she recognizes that Wilsonville has had vigorous public debate about growth in the past.
“From the perspective of somebody who lived here 25 years ago and remembers what it was like before we had Villebois, before we had Argyle Square, before we had a lot of things, I really feel that investing in getting rid of blight and having a vibrant Town Center that is a destination and provides places for people to go and do things and spend time together in community is the number one place that we need to be focusing our efforts right now,” she said.
However, she said any vision for the future of Wilsonville needs to include everyone in the community. This effort starts with trying to get as many people involved as possible.
“You know, people have very, very busy lives, particularly working families, and with affordability the way it is right now, I really want to be somebody that is a representative of working families on the council, particularly working mothers,” she said.
She believes the people who bring expertise and enthusiasm to the community are what make Wilsonville strong and has noticed that while campaigning.
“I want to bring perspective to decisions about growth, affordability, transportation and the kind of community we’re building for the next generation, and, because I’m a public employee, I’m used to working within these sort of bureaucratic systems where it can feel really hard to move the needle,” said Scritsmier. “But I have, over time, through serving on city boards and through my job, I’ve learned that sweet spot of setting a realistic goal that I can actually accomplish.”
For more information, visit adrienneforwilsonville.com.
